entries.title: Fix a flat tire
entries.summary: Replace or patch a punctured tube in about 15 minutes with tire levers and a pump.
steps: Remove the wheel: release the brake if needed, open the quick-release or thru-axle, and slide the wheel out.
Pull one side of the tire off the rim with tire levers and remove the tube.
Find the cause: run your fingers carefully along the inside of the tire for glass, thorns, or sharp spots.
Fit the new or patched tube: inflate it just enough to hold shape, seat the valve, and tuck it into the tire.
Work the tire bead back onto the rim with your thumbs — avoid levers here, they pinch tubes.
Inflate to the pressure printed on the tire sidewall and refit the wheel.

entries.title: Quiet squeaky brakes
entries.summary: Most brake squeal is contamination or pad alignment — both fixable at home.
steps: Clean the rims or rotors with isopropyl alcohol and a clean rag.
Check pad wear: replace pads worn past their indicator line.
Look for glazing: lightly sand glazed pads with fine sandpaper.
Align the pads so they meet the braking surface squarely.
If squeal continues, ride with light braking for a few minutes to bed the pads in.

entries.title: Chain care basics
entries.summary: A clean, lubed chain shifts better and stops gear skipping before it starts.
steps: Wipe the chain with a dry rag while backpedaling.
Apply one drop of bike-specific lube to each roller.
Backpedal a dozen turns so the lube works in, then wipe off the excess.
Check for wear with a chain checker — replace at 0.75% stretch.
If gears still skip after cleaning and lubing, the cassette or derailleur needs a shop adjustment — book a tune-up.

entries.title: Prep your bike for service drop-off
entries.summary: Five minutes of prep makes your service visit faster.
steps: Note your symptoms: when the problem happens and what it sounds like.
Remove accessories: lights, bags, GPS mounts, and locks.
Charge e-bike batteries to at least 50% and bring your key.
Arrive during drop-off hours, Tuesday to Saturday 9am to 6pm.
